description:
Receptionist/ Administrator

37 hours per week

Permanent

Southampton SSJ&I Service, London Road

Salary Scale: 20 - 21 (£25,947 - £26,305 per annum)

About Us

This is an exciting opportunity to join a dynamic Charity and Housing Association. The Society of St James (SSJ) has been working in Hampshire for over 50 years, delivering high impact, person-centred, accommodation services to adults and young people experiencing homelessness, problematic substance use and mental health problems. We believe that every person is of worth and we are prepared to take risks to house and support the most at risk and socially excluded members of society.

The Impact You'll Make

As one of the primary faces of the SSJ&I Alcohol and Drug Service, you will set the tone for every individual walking through our doors or reaching out over the phone. Operating with a calm, controlled, and welcoming manner, you will seamlessly guide clients to their appointments, pass queries to duty teams or care coordinators, and serve as a reassuring presence during critical moments in their recovery journey.

Working with a person-centred approach, you will directly support Southampton residents who are ready to make meaningful changes to their lives. By connecting service users to vital interventions-from therapeutic groups to prescribing and needle exchange services-and maintaining strong risk management standards, you will help create a safe environment where individuals feel heard, supported, and empowered to grow.

Through building genuine, trusting relationships with our client base, you will actively contribute to SSJ's core mission. Your everyday interactions will help cultivate a community of continuous growth and development, delivering real, positive change for both our service users and the wider organisation.

Who We're Looking For

Engaging & Personable: An innovative, tenacious individual who can connect meaningfully with service users and multitask effectively in a busy reception environment.

Empathetic & Resilient: Someone equipped with a self-reflective, motivated mindset who thrives both independently and as part of a collaborative team.

Flexible Team Member: A dedicated professional ready to work service-based across a 37-hour week, Monday - Friday working week.

Essential Qualities and Skills

Sector Knowledge & Experience: Experience working with this client group and a strong understanding of the impact of substance misuse on individuals, families, and communities. (Transferable skills from working with other disadvantaged groups will also be considered.)

Awareness of Resources: Up-to-date awareness of the issues this client group presents with, as well as knowledge of the relevant interventions, resources, and agencies available locally.

Core Competencies: Strong IT system skills, excellent multitasking capabilities, and proven expertise in risk management and building trusting relationships.

What we can offer you

We value and recognise our staff, offering some generous benefits, as well as the satisfaction of helping people at risk:
- A competitive annual leave entitlement of 25 days rising to 30 days, plus public holidays
- Flexible working options
- Buying additional annual leave
- Comprehensive induction and training
- Counselling, financial, personal support and health and wellbeing services via our Employee Assistance Programme
- Company cycle to work scheme
- Discounted laptops and computers with Jamie's Computers
- Electric Car Scheme
- Blue Light Card

SSJ are an equal opportunity employer and we encourage applicants from all backgrounds and walks of life.

At SSJ, we recognise the benefits of a supported workplace. SSJ is affiliated with Unite the Union. To learn more about their membership benefits or to sign up, you can visit their official website.

For an informal discussion about the role please contact us.

Application closing date: 5pm on Thursday 24th September 2026

Interview date: Wednesday 1st October 2026

Due to the high number of expected applicants, we do reserve the right to close this vacancy earlier.

Should you not hear from us within 14 days of the closing date, please assume you have been unsuccessful on this occasion.

About the Bookkeeper role

We are TC Group, the fastest-growing top 20 accountancy firm in the UK. We're business advisors and accountants, with over 30 years of experience we've honed our skills and developed our service offering to deliver a much wider range of bespoke support and advice to ambitious business owners and their businesses.

We have an exciting opportunity for a Bookkeeper in our Portsmouth office for TC Bulley Davey Ltd.

This role offers the opportunity to work closely with a diverse portfolio of clients, delivering high-quality bookkeeping support tailored to their individual needs. You will build strong client relationships while developing your technical skills and expertise, playing a key role in supporting clients and contributing to the overall success of the team.

Key responsibilities of a Bookkeeper will include:
- Carrying out bank reconciliations using accounting software
- Using automation software to accurately capture and post invoices
- Reconciling sales and purchase ledgers on a regular basis
- Keeping accounting software up to date with accurate financial records
- Preparing and filing VAT returns for a portfolio of clients
- Acting as a point of contact for bookkeeping queries
- Communicating directly with HMRC when necessary, undertaking general administration tasks

About you

We are looking for candidates with the following skills and experience:
- Minimum of three years' bookkeeping experience, ideally within an accountancy practice
- AAT qualified or qualified by experience
- Strong knowledge of Xero and exposure to QBO, Fathom, and Dext
- Able to work independently, liaise directly with clients, and collaborate effectively within a team
- Strong organisational and time management skills, with the ability to manage workload and meet tight deadlines under pressure
- High level of accuracy and attention to detail, alongside a passion for delivering excellent client service
- Enthusiastic about using software and technology to improve efficiency
- Presents themselves professionally in client interactions and demonstrates a positive, motivated, can-do attitude

Full benefits available for the Bookkeeper
- On site parking
- Pension scheme
- Private medical insurance after 5 years' service
- Cycle to work scheme
- Relaxed and friendly working environment
- Hybrid working between office and home after probationary period
- Group life assurance 4 x salary
- Social events
- Access to our employee benefits portal - GP and prescription services, cashback and vouchers on everyday purchases
- Employee Assistance Programme
- Employee Referral Bonus - we're always looking for talented individuals to join our team
- Regular training and development - continuous development and support not only for your professional qualifications but also for your personal goals and aspirations

About us

TC Group is growing and changing at quite a pace! We're an ambitious group of people with the same aim - to create a consistent, high-quality experience for our clients. Like us, our client list is growing - we're supporting more and more of the UK's ambitious business owners, SME's and large Corporations and it's a real team effort. We're helping them make courageous decisions to grow their businesses.

We always seek the best talent, looking for individuals who are technically brilliant, solution-focused and continually strive to be the best in class. Each member of our team plays an integral part in creating the unique feel and culture of our business, which in turn helps us continue to grow, develop and evolve. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome candidates from all backgrounds.

title: EHCP Coordinator
description:
EHCP Coordinator
Term-time only Minimum 30 hours/week over 39 weeks Spine Point 27 Based across 2 sites

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an EHCP Coordinator to join a dedicated Learning Support team, working across two sites. This is a rewarding role for someone passionate about ensuring young people with Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs) and High Needs receive the right support to thrive in their education.

Acting as Lead Professional, you will manage a caseload of students, coordinating the EHCP Annual Review process from start to finish and ensuring every student has the bespoke support they need to succeed.

Key responsibilities:

Coordinate and chair the EHCP Annual Review process for an assigned caseload, ensuring all statutory deadlines, legal frameworks, and quality standards are consistently met
Gather input from students, parents, and staff ahead of reviews, and complete post-review documentation within required timeframes
Ensure appropriate, individual support plans are established for EHCP students within 6 weeks of starting their programme
Liaise closely with external professionals - including speech and language therapists, occupational therapists, and physiotherapists - as well as Local Authorities and Statutory Assessment Teams
Work with curriculum, careers, admissions, and student services teams across both sites to ensure a joined-up approach to student support
Support students transitioning into or within the organisation, including attending school annual reviews, transition meetings, and welcome/enrolment events
Maintain accurate, up-to-date records across MIS platforms (e.g. ProSolutions, Pro-Monitor) and contribute to funding requests and Local Authority returns, including top-up funding applications
Provide cover for colleagues chairing annual reviews when needed, and support wider team training and development

What we're looking for:

Proven experience working within SEND/EHCP processes, ideally within a post-16, Further Education, or similar setting
Strong organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage a demanding caseload across multiple sites against statutory deadlines
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with confidence liaising across a wide range of stakeholders - parents, external agencies, and multi-disciplinary professional teams
A sound understanding of safeguarding principles and their application to vulnerable groups
A collaborative, proactive approach and genuine commitment to improving outcomes for young people with additional needs
A willingness and ability to travel between sites as required

What's on offer:

Local Government Pension Scheme
Employee assistance programme, including access to counselling support
Subsidised eye tests and prescription lenses for VDU users
Free on-site parking
Access to ongoing staff development and training funding
The opportunity to make a genuine, lasting difference in the lives of young people with additional needs

Aspire People Limited provides services as an Education Agency and an Education Employment Business. Aspire People is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of pupils and expects every candidate to share this commitment. Placements are subject, to appropriate Child Protection screening, including checks with former employers and the Disclosure and Barring Checks.

title: Client Servicing Coordinator
company: de Mellow & Co Financial Planning - Agency - Permanent
description:
Client Servicing Coordinator

At de Mellow & Co Financial Planning, we believe financial planning should be about people, not just numbers. As a family-run Chartered practice and Partner Practice of St. James's Place, we're passionate about helping our clients achieve financial confidence and security.

We're looking for someone who enjoys working with people and takes pride in getting the details right.

As a Client Servicing Coordinator, you'll work closely with our Financial Advisers to support their clients and keep things running smoothly behind the scenes. From preparing for client meetings and responding to queries, to submitting new business and following up outstanding actions, you'll play an important part in delivering a great client experience.

It's a varied role where you'll need to be organised, proactive and comfortable juggling priorities.

What will you be doing?

You'll be involved in a little bit of everything, including:
- Supporting Financial Advisers with their client relationships
- Communicating with clients by phone and email
- Preparing for client meetings
- Submitting new business and tracking progress
- Following up outstanding information and actions
- Keeping client records and systems up to date
- Liaising with providers and other teams
- Supporting the wider team with day-to-day administration

You don't need to know financial services.

Previous financial services experience or a financial qualification isn't essential. You might be an experienced administrator ready for your next step, a client-service professional looking for a new challenge, or simply have transferable experience from another professional environment.

We'll teach you the industry. What matters most to us is how you work.

We're looking for someone who is:

Collaborative - enjoys being part of a team, sharing knowledge and supporting others.

Determined - takes ownership, finds solutions and sees things through.

Committed - takes pride in doing a great job for our clients and colleagues.

You'll also need to be organised, have a good eye for detail and communicate confidently with different people.

Where could this take you?

You don't need to arrive knowing everything. We'll support you in building your financial services knowledge and developing your client-servicing skills, with the opportunity to take on more responsibility as you grow.

For the right person, there's potential to progress within the team and towards a Client Servicing Manager role over time.

Why us?

You'll be joining a close-knit team where everyone has an important part to play. We work collaboratively, share knowledge and support each other, while giving people the opportunity to take ownership and develop.

If you're looking for a role where you can learn, contribute and become an important part of a team, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Administrator
description: Island City Practice is looking for a motivated, organised, and detail-focused individual to join our team in a varied and rewarding administrative support role. Working as part of a multidisciplinary team, you will provide comprehensive secretarial, administrative, and data management support, helping to ensure the smooth and efficient delivery of high-quality patient care. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with strong organisational skills, attention to detail, and a commitment to delivering excellent patient support. In return, you will join a friendly and supportive team dedicated to providing outstanding care to our local community. Post details - 32 hours a week Monday: 09:00 - 17:00 Tuesday: 09:00 - 17:00 Wednesday: 09:00 - 18:00 Thursday: 09:00 - 18:00 Friday: Non-working day The role involves processing electronic and paper-based information accurately and in a timely manner, coding clinical information within patient records, and maintaining high standards of data quality in line with practice policies and procedures. You will liaise regularly with clinicians, administrative colleagues, and external healthcare providers, including secondary care and community services, using systems such as the Electronic Referral Service (ERS). The following are the core responsibilities of the Administrator. From time to time, additional duties may be required to support the needs of the practice, depending on workload and staffing requirements. Accurately code clinical information using SystmOne. Extract, interpret, and enter information from clinical correspondence and secondary care communications into patients' electronic health records. Process and code clinical results, ensuring all relevant information is recorded appropriately. Summarise patient records and manage the receipt and electronic integration of new patient notes. Maintain high standards of data quality and contribute to data quality improvement initiatives. Process patient referrals to external healthcare providers, including secondary care services, using the Electronic Referral Service (e-RS). Manage urgent referrals, Two Week Wait referrals, and Advice and Guidance requests, ensuring clinicians are kept informed and patient records are updated accordingly. Review, scan, code, and action incoming clinical and administrative correspondence in line with practice protocols. Liaise with patients and external organisations where required to support the efficient completion of referrals. Provide comprehensive administrative and secretarial support to the multidisciplinary team. Process incoming and outgoing mail, prepare correspondence, and undertake photocopying and document management tasks as required. Respond to administrative queries, perform system searches, and support clinical staff with a range of administrative duties. Manage the practice's general email inbox, prioritising, responding to, and distributing correspondence appropriately. Provide reception support during periods of staff absence or increased operational demand, as directed by management. Process requests for private services and medical reports in accordance with practice procedures. Handle incoming and outgoing telephone calls professionally, courteously, and compassionately, resolving queries or directing them to the appropriate person where necessary.
